messages:
emily (sales): FYI Acme's security team flagged a CAIQ item about log ownership/retention for a Private deployment. They want a clear matrix: what we collect, what they must collect, and where KMS keys are used. They specifically called out 'Audit logging', 'Application logs', and 'Network flow/egress'.
rajesh (security): Thanks — good catch. High-level: Redwood collects operational audit logs (control plane actions, tenant config changes) in the control plane. For Private (VPC/on-prem) customers, infrastructure-level logs (host OS, node-level GPU logs) are customer-managed unless they opt into our agent.
ben (solutions): Adding a quick mapping suggestion we can drop into the CAIQ response. Keep it concise:
- Control plane audit: Redwood (retained 90d by default, exportable to customer S3/GCS)
- Application request logs (request/response bodies): Customer controlled for private; hosted retains per TOS
- Model inference metrics (latency, tokens): Redwood (aggregated, PII removed)
- Network flow / VPC flow: Customer (we can forward to their SIEM)
olivia (eng): To clarify implementation: for Private with our agent installed, we can forward node logs to a customer endpoint (s3, syslog, or direct SIEM) and encrypt with customer-managed KMS if configured. If agent not used, customers must run the collector and provide endpoint.
emily (sales): Acme wants retention options (30/90/365) and proof for SIG. Can we provide a short statement that we support export and configurable retention for control plane logs?
rajesh (security): Yes — statement: "Redwood retains control plane audit logs for 90 days by default; archival and custom retention policies (30/90/365/adhoc) can be configured via export to a customer-managed storage bucket protected by their KMS." Use that in CAIQ L4/L5 mapping.
ben (solutions): I'll paste a tiny YAML snippet they can include in their CAIQ appendix to show configuration options:
```yaml
control_plane_logs:
  retention_default_days: 90
  export_supported: true
  export_destinations: ["s3","gcs","syslog","splunk_http"]
  kms_support: customer_managed|redwood_managed
```
olivia (eng): Note: for network egress logs we only capture what traverses our managed gateway. For fully private on-prem where traffic never hits our gateway, no network logs are captured by Redwood. Mention this edge case in the CAIQ answer.
emily (sales): Good — Acme also asked about evidence: screenshots or a runbook? They want something to attach to SIG.
rajesh (security): We can provide: (1) CAIQ response text + mapping table, (2) screenshot of export config from Console, (3) a short runbook snippet for enabling customer KMS on exports, and (4) sample SIEM forwarding config. I'll prepare the artifacts.
ben (solutions): I'll draft the CAIQ section and the shared-responsibility matrix. Quick suggested language for CAIQ Q: "Redwood is responsible for control-plane audit and aggregated inference telemetry; customer is responsible for application-level logs and host/node-level logs in Private deployments unless agent forwarding is enabled."
emily (sales): Perfect. Can someone own the POC step to demo export and KMS key rotation for Acme? They want a short call next week.
olivia (eng): I can run the demo. Suggest 30 min: show Console export -> S3 + KMS, then show Syslog forward to Splunk.
infra-bot: Ticket #RDW-5421 created: "Acme CAIQ - log ownership artifacts" assigned to @rajesh, @ben, @olivia. ETA: draft by Tue EOD.
rajesh (security): I'll own the CAIQ text and the retention policy statement. Ben please drop the matrix into the ticket. Olivia please confirm demo runbook by Monday.
emily (sales): Thx team :thumbsup: I'll reply to Acme with an ETA (Tue EOD) and propose two slots for the demo next week.
ben (solutions): One more note for CAIQ: call out encryption in transit + at rest, and reference our KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK) — small bullets are enough.
rajesh (security): Agreed. Also add the edge-case line Olivia mentioned about fully air-gapped on-prem. That avoids overclaiming.
emily (sales): Great. I'll post the CAIQ draft to the thread once Ben and Rajesh push to the ticket.
